newsitem.title: USA: USDA to unveil new Karnal Bunt rule this week.
newsitem.headline: USDA to unveil new Karnal Bunt rule this week.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department will unveil a new rule this week that will relax restrictions for the wheat fungus Karnal Bunt, a USDA official said Tuesday.
Mike Stefan, an official at USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, told a group of millers the department hoped to publish the interim rule in the Federal Register on Thursday.
The new regulation "pretty much follows along the trends of reducing restrictions," Stefan said.

Stefan said the rule changes the criteria by which USDA determines what areas will be regulated. The department will base its assessment strictly on bunted kernels instead of spores as it did last year.
Stefan said the change vastly would reduce the area under regulation.

For example, he said in California last year, 6,000 square miles were regulated, but that this year, USDA expects only to regulate about 800 miles in the state. He noted that the Imperial Valley would be completely removed from surveillance.
"The bottom line is that it reduces the area that we are regulating considerably," Stefan said.

He said the department also planned a technical follow-up rule that would review regulations on articles like farm tools. He also said USDA would host an international symposium on Karnal Bunt in Raleigh, N.C., August 17-20.
A little over a year ago, the wheat fungus was detected in seed that originated from Arizona, leading to a government quarantine in parts of California, Arizona, Texas and New Mexico.
Karnal Bunt, also called Stinking Smut, makes wheat smell bad and reduces yield and quality but does not pose a health risk.

Stefan said the government's initial reaction was very conservative and said they have been steadily racheting down the program. He said they recognized that the crop loss was minimal and the fungus seemed to be manageable by growers.
"Our greatest problem is we have to deal with our trading partners, both domestic and foreign," Stefan said.
